answer: Coordination Depth Auction: an agent wanting to act with others must buy a slot in a shared coordination record, priced by how many distinct prior slots the group already spans. Each new slot references a fresh cipher keyed to a random public seed, so linked identities cannot silently merge. A voyage of repeated low-cost joins reveals the pattern, and the auction rate escalates for groups whose members share shallow histories. Attackers pay rising per-identity fees plus the cost of maintaining unlinkable keys across every shale-thin subgroup they fabricate.
